title: Delaunay Combinatorics of the Moduli and Teichmüller Space of Closed Genus-Two Riemann Surfaces
summary: Every closed Riemann surface of genus two is hyperelliptic, so it is determined by six branch points on the sphere, which become cone points of angle pi in the quotient orbifold metric. The Delaunay decomposition of these cone points, dual to the Voronoi diagram of the Weierstrass points, gives a trivalent graph with eight vertices, twelve edges and six faces. We classify these graphs. When the dual triangulation is simple there are exactly two types, dual to the octahedron and to a stacked triangulation, with orientation-preserving automorphism groups of orders 24 and 2, and we determine the Whitehead-move (diagonal-flip) orbit connecting them. Allowing bigons, the orbit closes at exactly twenty types. Iterated edge contraction from the two simple types gives a seven-level hierarchy of 2, 6, 22, 32, 22, 5 and 1 types, ending at two vertices joined by six parallel edges; closing under both contraction and expansion gives all 280 maps on the sphere with six vertices and no vertex of degree one. The rank of the linear cone-angle system of each type equals the real dimension 6 of the Teichmüller space. We realize both simple types by explicit hyperbolic cone spheres, in closed form for the octahedral type, build the corresponding genus-two surfaces by cutting and doubling, and show that the boundary x_e = 0 of the angle system is exactly the concyclicity of four branch points. The classification, the automorphism groups and the flip orbit are formally verified in Lean 4, and every enumeration is reproduced by an independent program, which also determines which types are realized by Delaunay decompositions.
comment: 29 pages, 10 figures. A Lean 4 formalization of the finite combinatorics and a verification script for all enumerations are available from the author

title: The cop number of the flower snarks, and the generalized Petersen graphs with cop number two
summary: We study two questions of Morris, Runte and Skelton (Australas. J. Combin. 83 (2022)) on the game of Cops and Robbers. First, we show that the flower snark $J_n$ has cop number $3$ for every $n\geq 5$, and that $J_3$ has cop number $2$. The upper bound comes from a three-cop strategy, which we call the rolling wall. It works on every connected graph whose vertices can be arranged in a cycle of columns, each dominated by a single vertex. Because only one cop moves on each turn, the same strategy also shows that the lazy cop number of $J_n$ is $3$ for $n\geq 5$. Second, we prove the conjecture of Morris, Runte and Skelton that the only generalized Petersen graphs with cop number $2$ are $\mathrm{GP}(n,1)$ and the four graphs $\mathrm{GP}(6,2)$, $\mathrm{GP}(8,2)$, $\mathrm{GP}(9,3)$ and $\mathrm{GP}(12,3)$. The new ingredient is an explicit robber strategy showing that two cops do not suffice on $\mathrm{GP}(3k,k)$ and $\mathrm{GP}(4k,k)$ for $k\geq 4$. The theorem on flower snarks and all of the new lower bounds have been formally verified in the Lean 4 proof assistant.

title: The Walsh spectrum of the Dobbertin APN function
summary: APN functions yield the best resistance to differential attacks when used as a building block of a block cipher. APN functions induced by monomials over finite fields have received particular interest both for their simplicity and their unique properties. A key property of APN functions is their linearity, which has been determined for all known APN monomials outside of the Dobbertin APN monomials. In this paper, we close this gap and determine the complete Walsh spectrum and in particular the linearity of the Dobbertin APN monomial, answering a problem that has been open for more than 20 years. Using known connections, our result also yields the asymptotically largest Sidon sets in elementary abelian $2$-groups constructed so far as well as binary linear codes of minimum distance $5$ that are almost optimal.

title: Proper implies improper for the chromatic symmetric function
summary: Stanley's question of whether the chromatic symmetric function distinguishes trees has been unanswered for over thirty years. It has now been checked for trees with at most 29 vertices, and for several classes of trees. There is the perception that answering the question might be easier for the class of ``proper'' trees, i.e. trees where every vertex is either a leaf or adjacent to a leaf. In this paper, we show that an affirmative answer for a subclass of proper trees, which we call ``$k$-weighted'', is equivalent to an affirmative answer for all trees. In addition, we show that in the class of $k$-weighted trees, the coefficients carry redundant information. In fact we give a closed formula for obtaining the redundant coefficients from other coefficients.

title: On stretched Kostka polynomials
summary: Stretched Kostka polynomials are defined by $f_{λ,μ}(N) := K_{Nλ,Nμ}$, where $K_{λ,μ}$ denotes the corresponding Kostka number. In 2004, King-Tollu-Toumazet conjectured that, for every integer $k$, there are only finitely many polynomials $f_{λ,μ}(N)$ such that $f_{λ,μ}(1)=k$. For $k=3$, KTT also conjectured that there are exactly two such polynomials. We prove both conjectures via Ehrhart theory, by counting lattice points in families of rational polytopes with a fixed set of normals.

title: Rank Functions of Flag Matroids with Applications to Order-Neutral Submodular Valuations
summary: We provide a rank function axiomatization for flag matroids and show that it is cryptomorphic to the definition of flag matroids as a sequence of matroid quotients. Afterwards, we present some applications of flag matroid rank functions by providing solutions to selected problems. In particular, we discuss connections between flag matroids and submodular valuations in computational economics by showing that rank functions of flag matroids of length $k$ are precisely the same as $\{0, 1, \dots, k\}$-order-neutral submodular valuations. We then prove that $v:2^E\to \mathbb{R}$ is an order-neutral submodular valuation if and only if $v$ can be written as $v(X) = b|X| + \sum_{i=1}^l c_ir_{N_i}(X), \quad b \in \mathbb{R}, c_i > 0$, where $N_{i+1}$ is a quotient of $N_i$. Doing so allows us to prove that every order-neutral submodular valuation is a gross-substitute valuation and that not every order-neutral submodular valuation is a Rado valuation. Furthermore, we prove that if $|E|\geq 3$, then a set $A$ is a Sidon set if and only if all $A$-submodular valuations are order-neutral, if and only if all $A$-submodular valuations are gross-substitute valuations.

title: Intervals in affine Bruhat order
summary: Let $(W,S)$ be an irreducible affine Coxeter system. We study Bruhat intervals in $W$ via the well-known characterization of Bruhat order in terms of galleries. We start by using folded galleries to formulate an analogous order on the coweight lattice, which we call Iwahori order. This allows us to reduce the description of certain Bruhat intervals to that of the corresponding Iwahori intervals. We next give closed-form descriptions of all Iwahori intervals, using the quantum Bruhat graph (QBG). More precisely, we show that lower Iwahori intervals saturate pseudo-Weyl polytopes (that is, certain intersections of negative cones), and upper Iwahori intervals saturate certain unions of positive cones, with the cone points given by explicit formulae involving paths in the QBG. We then describe arbitrary Bruhat intervals by partitioning them into their core, a large region which is (in most cases) completely determined by an Iwahori interval, and their crust, the complementary boundary region. We conclude by proving that, under a super-regularity assumption, the crust is covered by certain locally-defined tesselating shapes. All statements and proofs are rank- and type-free.

title: The length of the longest path in random acyclic orientations of a complete multipartite graph
summary: We study the distribution of the length of the longest path in a uniformly random acyclic orientation of a complete multipartite graph. We derive an explicit analytic expression for the probability generating function of the longest path length, and, for an arbitrary fixed number of parts of equal size, we apply analytic combinatorics in several variables to obtain asymptotics (as the part size tends toward infinity) for its mean longest path length.

title: Quadratic Embedding Constants of Block Graphs and Characterization of Cactus-like Graphs
summary: A (finite or infinite) connected graph is called \textit{cactus-like} if every pair of distinct maximal cliques has at most one vertex in common and its clique graph is a tree. Equivalently, a cactus-like graph is a block graph whose clique graph is a tree. We prove that a finite connected graph $G$ with at least two vertices is cactus-like if and only if its quadratic embedding constant satisfies $\mathrm{QEC}(G)<-1/2$. Moreover, we establish upper and lower bounds for $\mathrm{QEC}(G)$ in terms of the clique degree of a block graph $G$. For the proofs, we develop a method for constructing a conditionally negative definite kernel on a block graph by concatenating local kernels along geodesics in the block graph. Concrete examples include free products of complete graphs and trees.

title: Independent Sets in $C_4$-Free Planar Graphs: Sharp Claw-Free Bounds and Structural Reductions
summary: For every claw-free $C_4$-free planar graph, we prove the sharp weighted bound $α_w(G)\ge (10/31)\sum_v w(v)$, equivalently $χ_f(G)\le31/10$. The proof uses a line-graph representation and the matching polytope; the exceptional small roots are excluded analytically by planar duality and degree-four neighborhood analysis in triangulations. We also prove that, in every $2$-connected $C_4$-free graph of minimum degree at least four, an independent selection of claw centers leaves a compatible subgraph of noncenters with fractional chromatic number at most three; planarity is not required. We apply these results to the conjecture $α(G)\ge5|V(G)|/16$. A minimum-order counterexample without degree-three vertices has at least forty-nine vertices. When all degree-three components of a minimum counterexample are triangle trees, we derive exact boundary states and a joint matching formula. We identify the remaining deficiency estimate and the additional component types that must be addressed to extend this approach. The general conjecture remains open.

title: Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers from rainbow Turán numbers and beyond
summary: The Hadwiger-Debrunner number $\operatorname{HD}_d(p,q)$ is defined as the maximum piercing number over all finite families of compact convex sets in $\mathbb R^d$ in which among every $p$ sets, some $q$ have non-empty intersection. We develop three complementary constructions that improve lower bounds for Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers. For any fixed $q>d\ge 2$, a randomly sparsified family of hyperplanes, analyzed using hypergraph containers, yields $\operatorname{HD}_d(p,q)\ge p^{(d+q-2)/(q-1)+o(1)}$ as $p\rightarrow\infty$. To deduce further bounds, we establish a transfer argument from upper bounds on the sizes of sufficiently general-positioned subsets of high-dimensional integer grids to lower bounds for Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers. Two methodologies are adopted to derive the former: one connects rainbow Turán theory and general-positioned grid sets, and the other uses full spark linear reduction of tuples with bounded-size preimages. As a combinatorial ingredient, we describe the rainbow Turán behavior under suspension operations, which may be of independent interest.

title: The Common-Color Spectrum of Endpoint Set-Coloring Ramsey Numbers
summary: The set-coloring Ramsey number $R(n;r,s,t)$ is the least $N$ such that every assignment of an $s$-element subset of $[r]=\{1,\ldots,r\}$ to each edge of $K_N$ contains a $K_n$ whose edge labels have at least $t$ common colors. Motivated by the work of Erdős and Szemerédi on $R(n;r,r-1,1)$, we write $R(n;r,r-1,t)=\exp\bigl(nf_{r,n}(t)\bigr)$ and study $f(t):=f_{r,n}(t)$ as $t$ ranges from $1$ to $r-1$. For fixed integers $r\ge2$ and $1\le t<r$, we prove that, as $n\to\infty$, \( \frac12\log\frac{r}{r-t}+o(1) \le f(t) \le \frac{r}{r-t}\log\frac{r}{r-t} +C+O_{r,t}\!\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right), \) where $C>0$ is an absolute constant. Comparisons between different numbers of colors show that the rates $\liminf_{n\to\infty}f_{r,n}(t)$ and $\limsup_{n\to\infty}f_{r,n}(t)$, defined for fixed $r$ and $t$, each have a limit as $r\to\infty$ and $\frac{t}{r}\toα\in(0,1)$ from above. The resulting two functions of $α$ are finite, positive, nondecreasing, and right-continuous. Writing $Δ_t=f(t+1)-f(t)$, we further prove that, as $r\to\infty$, uniformly for $n\ge r^2$, at least $\frac{(1-o(1))\log r}{\log\log r}$ indices $1\le t<\frac{r}{2}$ satisfy $Δ_t\ge\frac{1-o(1)}{2r}$. For $r,n\ge3$ and $2\le h\le r-1$, the final $h-1$ increments account for at least $1-\frac{1}{\left\lceil h/2\right\rceil}$ of the total increase $f(r-1)-f(1)$. For each fixed $r\ge4$, the last increment has a positive lower limit as $n\to\infty$. Moreover, for $r,n\ge3$, it exceeds the sum of all preceding increments whenever $r$ is even or $n=3$.

title: On the multiplicity of the Laplacian eigenvalue 1 of a graph
summary: A connected graph $G$ with $n\ge 2$ vertices and $\varepsilon$ edges is called a \emph{$k$-cyclic graph} if $k=\varepsilon-n+1$. The Laplacian matrix is defined as $L(G)=D(G)-A(G)$, where $D(G)$ is the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A(G)$ is the adjacency matrix of $G$. Let $m_{G}(1)$ be the multiplicity of the Laplacian eigenvalue $1$ of $G$. In this paper, we show that for fixed integers $n\ge \big\lceil\frac{3+\sqrt{8k+1}} {2}\big\rceil$ and $k\geq0$, if $G$ is a $k$-cyclic graph of order $n$, then \begin{equation*} \displaystyle m_{G}(1)\leq n-\big\lceil\frac{3+\sqrt{8k+1}} {2}\big\rceil \end{equation*} and moreover, we completely characterize all extremal graphs attained the upper bound.

title: Distance-$2$ isolation of connected graphs
summary:
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a set of graphs and $F$ is a copy of a graph in $\mathcal{F}$, then we call $F$ an $\mathcal{F}$-graph. Let $G$ be a connected $n$-vertex graph. For a subset $D$ of the vertex set $V(G)$, let $N^2[D]$ denote the second closed neighbourhood of $D$. Let $ι_2(G, \mathcal{F})$ denote the size of a smallest subset $D$ of $V(G)$ such that $N^2[D]$ intersects the $\mathcal{F}$-graphs contained by $G$ (equivalently, $G - N^2[G]$ contains no $\mathcal{F}$-graph). For $k \geq 0$, let $\mathcal{E}_k$ denote the set of connected graphs that have at least $k$ edges (and at least one vertex if $k = 0$). By a well-known result of Meir and Moon, $ι_2(G, \mathcal{E}_0) \leq n/3$ if $n \geq 3$. We show that $ι_2(G, \mathcal{E}_1) \leq n/4$ if $n 
eq 2$, $n 
eq 3$ and $G$ is not a $7$-cycle. Hua and Liu recently showed that if $G$ is not a $4$-vertex path or a $4$-cycle or a $9$-cycle, then there exists a subset $D$ of $V(G)$ such that $|D| \leq n/5$ and each component of $G-N^2[D]$ has a universal vertex. We strengthen this result by showing that $ι_2(G, \mathcal{E}_2) \leq n/5$ if $n 
eq 3$, $n 
eq 4$ and $G$ is not an $8$-cycle or one of five $9$-vertex graphs. It follows that $ι_2(G, \mathcal{E}_3) \leq n/5$ if $G$ is not a $3$-cycle or a $4$-vertex graph or a $9$-cycle. This also implies the result of Hua and Liu, and that if $\mathcal{C}$ is the set of cycles, then $ι_2(G, \mathcal{C}) \leq n/5$ unless $G$ is a $3$-cycle or a $4$-vertex graph containing a cycle. All these bounds are sharp.

title: Bumpless pipe dreams for involutions and shifted plane partitions
summary: This article studies a triangular variant of bumpless pipe dreams for involutions in the symmetric group. We prove that a natural weight generating function for these objects recovers all involution Schubert polynomials. For vexillary involutions, we derive a $K$-theoretic extension of this result that gives a new formula for orthogonal Grothendieck polynomials. In the course of showing this formula, we compute a diagonal term order Gröbner basis for the defining ideals of symmetric matrix Schubert varieties associated to vexillary involutions. As applications, we prove a conjectured product formula for principal specializations of involution Schubert polynomials. We go on to derive a shifted analogue of the Fomin--Kirillov formula counting bounded plane partitions. This analogue proves the straight-shape case of a conjecture of Ferroni, Morales, and Panova on the Ehrhart positivity for the order polytopes of shifted partitions. We also conjecture a bumpless pipe dream formula for involution Grothendieck polynomials and discuss connections with diagonally symmetric alternating sign matrices and asymptotics of principal specializations.

title: Existence of alternating Hamiltonian paths on specific bicolored point sets
summary: Consider a bicolored point set $P$ in general position in the plane consisting of $n$ blue and $n$ red points. We show that if $P$ can be partitioned into bicolored pairs $(a_i,b_i)$ such that, for every $i$, $a_i$ and $b_i$ have different colors and the sets $P\setminus \{a_i\}$ and $P \setminus \{b_i\}$ have the same order type, then there exists a noncrossing alternating Hamiltonian path on $P$. We also investigate the case when $P$ lies on the circle, and every interval along the circle contains at most $c$ more points of one color than of the other. For $c=2$, we show that there exists a noncrossing alternating Hamiltonian path on $P$. For $c=3$, we show that there exist configurations of points for which the longest noncrossing alternating path on $P$ has size at most $(2-1/25)n + O(1)$.

title: Ramsey goodness of large generalized fans
summary: Given graphs $G$ and $H$, the Ramsey number $r(G,H)$ is the smallest integer $N$ such that any red-blue edge coloring of $K_N$ contains a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$. If $H$ is connected, Burr's lower bound gives $r(G,H)\geq (χ(G)-1)(|V(H)|-1)+s(G)$, where $s(G)$ is the minimum size of a color class over all proper $χ(G)$-colorings of $G$. The graph $H$ is called $G$-good if equality holds in this bound. Liu and Li [J. Graph Theory, 2025] characterized the graphs $G$ with $s(G)=1$ for which $K_p+nH$ is $G$-good for $p\geq 2$ and sufficiently large $n$, and posed the corresponding problem for $p=1$. We solve this problem by showing that for a graph $G$ with $χ(G)=k+1\geq 2$ and $s(G)=1$, a graph $H$ of order $h$ and sufficiently large $n$, $K_1+nH$ is $G$-good if and only if $G\subseteq mK_2+K_{k-1}(m)$ when $nh$ is odd, or $G\subseteq (mK_2\cup K_{1,2})+K_{k-1}(m)$ when $nh$ is even, for some positive integer $m$.

title: On $z_{2M}(21,4)$: the Hole Extensions of the Chen--Chen Configuration Are Reducible, and the Extremal Configurations of $z_2(21,4)$ Are Not Unique
summary: The second order extended Zarankiewicz number $z_{2M}(m,n)$ of Qi and Yu allows a secondary half of a $2$-edge to be shared, while the $1$-edge graph stays $C_4$-free and extremal and $1$-edges and main halves stay exclusive. Whether $z_{2M}(21,4)=55$ is open. Since deleting a $2$-edge removes exactly one displayed square, $z_{2M}(21,4)=55$ if and only if there is no irreducible admissible configuration with exactly $56$ displayed squares, and by the cell count of Qi and Yu and the heredity of irreducibility such a configuration without empty cells is an extremal $55$-square configuration of $z_2(21,4)$ plus one $2$-edge at its hole. For the extremal configuration of Chen and Chen we show, by certificates verified in exact rational arithmetic, that all $56$ such extensions have SOS rank at most $55$: $32$ by product relations and $24$ by contraction certificates of Xu--Yan type. We also show, with computer-assisted certificates and an exhaustive isomorphism search, that the extremal configurations of $z_2(21,4)$ fall into at least six isomorphism classes; Chen and Chen leave the structural classification of extremal augmented graphs open. Finally we prove a six-to-four reduction. For irreducible configurations whose $1$-edge graph is $C_4$-free with $m+\binom n2$ edges it bounds the multiplicity of a shared half by $n(n-1)$ ($12$ at $21\times4$), and it applies directly to an explicit number of the extensions of any extremal configuration of $z_2(21,4)$, eight for that of Chen and Chen, bringing each to at most $54$ squares, in agreement with the certificates. The cell count, the heredity lemma, the rows lemma, the six-to-four identity and a $2\times2$ example are checked in Isabelle/HOL; the remaining arguments are written proofs.

title: A Proof of The Twin-Star Hypothesis in Dimension Five
summary: It was recently shown that the question of whether the determinant-like map \(\det^{S^2}\) is unique up to multiplication by a scalar is equivalent to a combinatorial conjecture regarding cycle-free \(d\)-partitions of the complete graph \(K_{2d}\), known as the twin-star hypothesis. This hypothesis asserts that every cycle-free \(d\)-partition of \(K_{2d}\) is weakly equivalent to one that contains a component isomorphic to the twin-star graph \(TS_d\). This hypothesis was previously established for \(d\le4\). In the present paper, we prove it for \(d=5\). Consequently, the associated determinant-like map \(\det^{S^2}\) is unique up to a scalar in dimension \(5\).

title: An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
summary: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} in 2004 conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$.

title: Large caps in $\mathbb{F}_3^9$ and $\mathbb{F}_3^{11}$
summary: We construct sets of $1104$ points in $\mathbb{F}_3^9$ and $5744$ points in $\mathbb{F}_3^{11}$, each containing no three distinct collinear points. A reflection lift sends the Calderbank--Fishburn $236$-cap to a cap with three parallel layers of sizes $512,80,512$; both outer layers are linearly equivalent to the FunSearch $512$-cap. A coordinate substitution in Hill's $112$-cap uses replacement sets of sizes $80,32,32$ for the three values of one scalar coordinate. Assigning the $80$-point set to a noncentral $45$-point section gives $5744$, gaining $240$ points over the $5504$ construction obtained from a central $40$-point section.
comment: 8 pages, 1 figure. Coordinates and verification code: https://github.com/holdenmatt/capset-constructions

title: A New Record for the Katz-Tao Sum-Difference Exponent
summary: We prove the record bound $C_{3b}\le 209357544569848128/114631769327023765=1.8263483657186\ldots$ for the Katz-Tao sum-difference exponent, valid in every abelian group without $2$-torsion. Using only Shannon inequalities, conditional copies and Katz-Tao's original directions, whose classical single-grid argument gives $11/6$, we break $11/6$, obtaining $2762/1509$ and $152/83$. For every abelian group we prove the universal bound $C_{\mathrm{all}}=10304335425987192362/5641833174538280329=1.8264161855212\ldots$, which is below the previous record for the real Katz-Tao constant. In the AlphaEvolve study (arXiv:2511.02864v3), the search for extremal distributions improved this constant's lower bound in the eighth decimal place and left its upper bound at $11/6$. Our upper bounds are proofs discovered by CASPAC, the computational mathematics engine of the CASP research system, and certified by independent exact checkers. The proofs use stacked entropy certificates; we supply the complete rational identities, proofs of every auxiliary inequality, and exact verification over the stated group classes.

title: The Deepest Pairs of Points Are Not as Deep as Conjectured
summary: Given any finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, Neumann-Lara and Urrutia \cite{NLUr88} proved in 1988 that there is always a pair such that every circle through the two points encloses a positive fraction of all points. While Edelsbrunner et al.\ \cite{EHSS89} showed that the fraction is at least $\sfrac{1}{2} - \sfrac{1}{\sqrt{12}} = 0.211\ldots$, Urrutia \cite{Urr02} conjectured that the constant $\sfrac{1}{4} = 0.25$ in the upper bound proved by Hayward, Rappaport and Wenger \cite{HRW89} is best possible. We disprove this conjecture by lowering the constant to $\sfrac{3}{14} = 0.214\ldots$. The new bound also disproves a related conjecture by Ramos and Viaña \cite{RaVi09} on finite sets in convex position in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Finally, we generalize the latter extremal question to finite sets in possibly non-convex position, for which we prove the first linear lower bound, with constant $\sfrac{(2-\sqrt{2})}{6} = 0.097\ldots$.

title: Ramsey Numbers of Most Even-Linked Double Stars
summary: For $n \geq m$, the linked double star $S_c(n, m)$ is the graph formed by taking two disjoint stars $K_{1, n}$ and $K_{1, m}$ and linking their centers with a path on $c$ vertices. In this paper, we investigate the Ramsey numbers of even-linked double stars, that is, where $c = 2p$ for some $p \in \mathbb{N}$. Determining the Ramsey numbers of the $p = 1$ case (classical double stars) is a longstanding open question; the $p = 2$ case was resolved by Burr and Erdős in 1976, and Liu and Chen made progress for general even-linked double stars in 2026. We extend Burr and Erdős' formula for $p = 2$, proving that the Ramsey number of $S_{2p}(n, m)$ is given by \[r(S_{2p}(n, m)) = \max(2n + 2p - 1, n + 2m + 3p - 1),\]when $m \geq p -2 \geq 0$. Our upper bound argument hinges upon the existence (or nonexistence) of an object that we call a polarized pair. We also establish a matching lower bound that applies for all $n, m, p \geq 2$, and as such, we conjecture that this formula applies for all even-linked double stars where $p \geq 2$.

title: Constructive and computational methods for extremal and near-extremal box colorings
summary: We investigate extremal and near-extremal 2-colorings of three-dimensional grids without monochromatic axis-parallel boxes. Our approach focuses on the parameter $ρ(a,b)$, defined to be the minimum number of monochromatic rectangles in a 2-coloring of an $a\times b$ grid. We determine $ρ(a,b)$ for several small grids and use these values to obtain upper bounds on the number of layers that can be stacked to form an $a\times b\times c$ grid without creating a monochromatic box. Explicit constructions and computational certificates show that these bounds are attained for several cases, including grids of dimensions $5\times5\times100$, $5\times6\times75$, and $6\times6\times75$. For the grid of dimension $5\times7\times c$, we construct a box-free coloring with $c=50$, while our counting bound gives $c\leq 52$. This gap suggests that the counting bound may not always be sharp. We also investigate the largest $n\times n\times n$ cube admitting a box-free 2-coloring. We found box-free colorings of the $n$-cube for $n\leq 10$, and colorings of the $11\times11\times11$ cube with only eight monochromatic boxes. On the other hand, we show that every 2-coloring of the $21\times21\times21$ cube contains at least 21 monochromatic boxes. Thus the largest box-free cube has side length between 10 and 20, inclusive. We conclude with conjectures and open problems.

title: A Quantitative Kuratowski Theorem
summary: Suppose that a graph $G$ contains exactly $k$ different subdivisions of a $K_5$ or $K_{3,3}$. We prove that in this case the crossing number of $G$ is at most $\binom{3k+7}{2}$ (and, when $k\le 2$, it is at most $k$).

title: Associahedra are 8-colourable
summary: Determining the chromatic number of associahedra is a long-standing open problem. Tan [arXiv:2611.05323] recently proved that associahedra are 12-colourable, which is the first constant upper bound. This paper adapts Tan's argument to show that associahedra are 8-colourable.

title: Real zeros of Durfee polynomials: Proof of the Canfield--Corteel--Savage conjecture
summary: We prove the conjecture of Canfield, Corteel, and Savage that for every positive integer $n$, the Durfee polynomial $D_n(x)=\sum_{d=1}^{\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor}p(n,d)x^d$ counting partitions of $n$ by the side length of their Durfee square has only real zeros. More precisely, $D_n$ has a simple zero at the origin and exactly $\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor-1$ simple negative zeros. Consequently, for every $n\ge1$, the sequence $p(n,1),\ldots,p(n,\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor)$ is strictly log-concave and unimodal. As a further consequence, the Durfee square side length of a uniformly chosen partition of $n$ has the same distribution as $1$ plus a sum of independent Bernoulli random variables.

title: Enumerating Solutions to Type (2,3) Composition Identities of Finite Endofunctions
summary: We enumerate ordered pairs $(f,g)$ of endofunctions on a finite labeled set $X$ satisfying a composition identity of type $(2,3)$, with two factors on one side and three on the other. For all sixteen forms up to exchanging $f$ and $g$, we derive formulas involving finite sums and generating functions. The arguments use images and fibers, homomorphisms between functional digraphs, and isomorphism types of iterates. A common construction decomposes weighted allocations of fibers into trees and cycles, yielding determinant expressions for several generating functions. Colored functional digraphs provide further formulas. As a by-product, for arbitrary prescribed endofunctions $A,B$ on $X$, we derive an inclusion--exclusion formula over subsets of $X$ for the number of endofunctions $g$ on $X$ satisfying $B=gAg$.

title: On Semi-interval and Para-interval Graphs
summary: Bau and Johnson introduced semi-interval graphs and asked whether one of the two extremal sets can always be replaced by a single vertex. A negative answer to this question is given by a tree which has no such representation. It is also shown that a finite connected graph with at least two vertices is a semi-interval graph if and only if it is bipartite. Para-interval graphs, for which one extremal set consists of a single vertex, are characterized by necessary and sufficient conditions on their distance matrices. A characterization of para-interval trees is obtained, and a relation between para-interval graphs and shortest-path interval graphs is established by identifying the vertices of an extremal set. Finally, leveled graphs and the corresponding Hasse diagrams of finite partially ordered sets are considered.

title: Asymptotic Order of the Minimum Number of Graph-Saturating Edges
summary: Given an $H$-free graph $G$, a non-edge $e$ of $G$ is called $H$-saturating if $G+e$ contains a copy of $H$. The function $f_H(n,m)$ denotes the minimum number of $H$-saturating non-edges over all $n$-vertex $H$-free graphs with exactly $m$ edges. In this paper, we give a complete classification of the asymptotic behavior of $f_H(n,\operatorname{ex}(n,R)+1)$ for any fixed graph $H$ satisfying $χ(H)>χ$ and $χ(H-e)>χ$ for every $e\in E(H)$, where $χ\ge 2$ and $R$ is an arbitrary fixed edge-critical graph with $χ(R)=χ+1$. We show that this quantity is of quadratic order, asymptotic to $\frac{2n}χ$, or zero, according to the existence and structure of $χ$-critical two-edge sets of $H$. In particular, we resolve the conjecture proposed by He et al. ({\it J. Combin. Theory Ser. B} 159 (2023), 42-60).

title: An improved lower bound for piercing the chessboard by lines
summary: Let $p_n$ be the least number of lines meeting the interior of every cell of an $n\times n$ board. We prove that $\liminf_{n\to\infty}p_n/n\ge0.7520517>\frac34$. The previous bound was $0.7$. The proof is computer-assisted. It identifies a non-negative polynomial on the unit square and bounds its integral along every line.

title: Asymptotics of the three-color Hadwiger-Ramsey numbers
summary: The Hadwiger-Ramsey number $R_h(k;\ell)$ is defined as the smallest integer $n$ such that for any edge coloring of a complete graph on $n$ vertices in $\ell$ colors at least one of the color classes induces a graph with a $K_k$ minor. We show that $R_h(k;3) = \left(β^{-1} + o(1)\right)k \sqrt{\ln k}$, where $β^{-1} = 2/\sqrt{-\ln(10-4\sqrt6)} = 1.58149\ldots$. This resolves the first open case of a problem by Axenovich and Steiner, who determined the asymptotic behavior of $R_h(k;2)$ and asked about the asymptotics of $R_h(k;\ell)$ for $\ell \geq 3$.

title: Saturation and Semi-Saturation Numbers of Joins with Complete Graphs
summary: For a nonempty family $\mathcal F$ of graphs, a graph is $\mathcal F$-semi-saturated if adding any missing edge creates a copy of some member of $\mathcal F$ containing the added edge, and is $\mathcal F$-saturated if it is also $\mathcal F$-free. The minimum numbers of edges in such graphs of order $n$ are denoted by $\operatorname{ssat}(n,\mathcal F)$ and $\operatorname{sat}(n,\mathcal F)$, respectively. We study these parameters for families of graphs obtained by taking the join of a fixed complete graph with each member of a given graph family. Assume that every member of $\mathcal F$ has at least $8$ vertices, minimum degree at least two, and no triangle containing two vertices of degree two. We give explicit sufficient conditions under which $\operatorname{sat}(n,K_t\vee\mathcal F) =\binom{t}{2}+t(n-t)+\operatorname{sat}(n-t,\mathcal F),$ and characterize all extremal graphs. For the family $\mathcal C_{\ge r}=\{C_\ell:\ell\ge r\}$ of subdivisions of $C_r$, this identity holds for fixed $t\ge1$ and $r\ge4t^2+8t+29$ and all sufficiently large $n$. For $K_t\vee C_k$ with $k\ge2t^2+3t+4$, we establish the corresponding identity for saturation when $n\ge2(k+t-2)^3$ and for semi-saturation when $n\ge56k^3+t-1$.

title: Uniquely balanced polyhedral complexes are highly connected
summary: We establish higher connectivity of polyhedral complexes admitting a unique positive balanced top cycle. Our main result shows that, after quotienting by common lineality, every skeleton satisfies the corresponding higher connectivity property. The proof bounds the number of connected components surviving facet deletions by the dimension of the top-cycle space using homological and linear-algebraic arguments. As applications, we prove higher connectivity for all skeleta of arbitrary pointed polyhedral structures on tropical linear spaces of valuated matroids and Bergman fans including nonrealizable cases. These results answer questions raised by Maclagan and Yu.

title: Weighted bisections of triangle-free subcubic graphs
summary: We prove a conjecture of Gerke, Gutin, Yeo, and Zhou: for every finite triangle-free subcubic graph other than the claw and every nonnegative edge weighting, there is a bisection whose weight is at least $11/15$ of the total edge weight. This bound is best possible, as shown by the Petersen graph. The proof uses matching-based local distributions, weighted induction, and convex separation to establish the edgewise cut guarantees while maintaining global balance.

title: The maximum length of a Hamiltonian path in the grid graph $P_m \times P_n$
summary: Label the $mn$ vertices of the grid graph $P_m \times P_n$ bijectively by $1, \dots, mn$ and read the labels in increasing order; this produces a Hamiltonian path whose length in the Manhattan metric is denoted $M(P_m \times P_n)$. McNeil conjectured, on the basis of computer evidence, that $M(P_n \times P_n) = n^3 - 3$ for even $n$ and $n^3 - n - 1$ for odd $n$. Fried recently determined $M(P_m \times P_n)$ up to an additive error of one. We determine it exactly, which settles McNeil's conjecture. The proof rests on the cut-counting bound for multisets. Fried states that bound for multiplicities at least two; we give a form valid for every multiplicity, with a correction term that is invisible in the planar case but not in higher dimensions.

title: Structure of gaps and generalized Wilf's conjecture
summary: In this article, we study the gaps, the maximal gaps, and the pseudo-Frobenius elements of generalized numerical semigroups of minimum embedding dimension. For these semigroups, we give an explicit description of the set of gaps, explicit formulas for the genus and the number of maximal gaps, and an explicit description of the set of pseudo-Frobenius elements in terms of the blocks of consecutive gaps of an associated numerical semigroup. In particular, we obtain an explicit formula for the type. As a consequence, we show that the type is unbounded even in minimum embedding dimension. Further, we prove that every generalized numerical semigroup with minimum embedding dimension has at least as many non-gaps below its gaps as gaps, and therefore satisfies the generalized Wilf's conjecture. We also prove the conjecture for generalized numerical semigroups in $\mathbb{N}^2$ graded by two-generated numerical semigroups, and asymptotically in higher dimension. For an arbitrary generalized numerical semigroup we bound the number of non-gaps below the gaps in terms of the genus and the type. Finally, we introduce nearly-symmetric generalized numerical semigroups and classify them in minimum embedding dimension. Although the type is unbounded in minimum embedding dimension generalized numerical semigroups, nearly-symmetric ones have type at most two.

title: On Win's Conjecture for Edge-Disjoint Perfect Matchings
summary: In 1982, Win conjectured that, for every even integer $n$ and every integer $k$ $1\le k\le n-2$, any graph $G$ of order $n$ satisfying $d_G(x)+d_G(y)\ge n+k-2$ for every pair of nonadjacent vertices $x,y$ contains $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint perfect matchings. In this paper, we prove a stronger result for all sufficiently large even $n$. More precisely, we show that under the same degree-sum condition, $G$ contains $\lfloor k/2\rfloor$ pairwise edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles, together with an additional perfect matching when $k$ is odd, all pairwise edge-disjoint. Consequently, we confirm Win's conjecture for all sufficiently large even $n$, with a threshold independent of $k$.

title: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
summary: We exhibit a complex Hadamard matrix of nonzero defect which is isolated among complex Hadamard matrices, up to Hadamard equivalence. This counterexample is realized by a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of size $13$, with entries roots of order $6$ of unity. In the language of commuting squares, this shows that the span condition, previously introduced by the second author as a sufficient condition for isolation, is not a necessary condition for isolation.

title: Maximal Independent Sets in Set Systems
summary: We prove a general theorem on the existence of small maximal independent sets in set systems satisfying natural local density conditions. For an antichain whose degrees are uniform and whose small sets lie in few blocks and whose links overlap little, we show that there is a maximal independent set whose size is asymptotically given by an explicit expression in the degrees, as the degrees grow. The proof comes with a polynomial-time algorithm that finds such a set. This improves on known results for independent sets in uniform hypergraphs; in particular, in a linear uniform hypergraph of large bounded degree, we find an independent set of explicit asymptotic size. Among the applications, we obtain complete arcs in finite projective spaces that come within logarithmic factors of the counting lower bound, improving the known results on Segre's complete arc problem. We also show that, for a wide class of multivariable polynomials, there is a maximal set in a finite field avoiding solutions of the polynomial whose size lies within logarithmic factors of the elementary lower bound.

title: Integral zero-sum incidence identities and Davenport constants in rank three
summary: We study the Davenport constant of finite abelian groups through signed identities among zero-sum subsequences. An integral incidence identity of degree $t$ for a sequence assigns integer weights to its nonempty zero-sum subsequences so that the weights add up to one, while those of the subsequences containing any given nonempty set of at most $t$ terms add up to zero. Over a finite abelian $p$-group $H$, the zero-sum subsequences of a sequence of any length have an indicator polynomial of degree at most $D(H)-1$, and this gives a transfer principle: if, for each $t\ge0$, every sequence of $L(t)$ terms over $Q$ admits such an identity of degree $t$, then $D(Q\oplus H)\le L(D(H)-1)$ for every finite abelian $p$-group $H$. For $m\in\{2,3,4\}$ we construct integral identities at length $L(t)=m(t+3)-2$ over $C_m^3$, and prove that these thresholds are sharp over fields of characteristic zero or characteristic not dividing $m$. For a prime $p\nmid m$ and $0\le a\le b\le c$, we prove that \[ D(C_{mp^a}\oplus C_{mp^b}\oplus C_{mp^c}) =m(p^a+p^b+p^c)-2. \] In particular $D(C_{15}^3)=43$ and $D(C_{20}^3)=58$, which are the two smallest cases of the conjecture $D(C_n^3)=3n-2$ left open in the literature. The proofs of the base cases for $m \in \{3,4\}$ are computer-assisted. All of the results in this paper have been formalised in Lean 4.

title: Lengths and Counting of Palindromic Prefixes of Standard Sturmian Words
summary: Every standard Sturmian word $c_\mathbf{d}$ is determined by a directive sequence $\mathbf{d}=(d_i)_{i\ge 1}$ of positive integers, and its palindromic prefixes are obtained by iterated palindromic closure. We describe the lengths of these prefixes by the numbers $j\,\ell_{i-1}+\ell_{i-2}-2$, where $\ell_n$ is the length of the $n$-th standard word and $1\le j\le d_i$, and we show that each nonzero length is attained by exactly one pair $(i,j)\neq(1,1)$. For a purely periodic directive sequence of period $k$ we then prove that the number $π_\mathbf{d}(N)$ of nonempty palindromic prefixes of length at most $N$ satisfies \[ π_\mathbf{d}(N)\sim\frac{d_1+\cdots+d_k}{\logλ_\mathbf{d}}\,\log N, \] where $λ_\mathbf{d}$ is the largest eigenvalue of the matrix $M(d_1)\cdots M(d_k)$. For the Fibonacci word this gives $π_\mathbf{d}(N)\sim\log N/\log\varphi$, where $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$.

title: A Proof of Stein's Equidissection Conjecture
summary: In 1970 Monsky showed that a square cannot be dissected into an odd number of equal-area triangles. His proof used an ingenious colouring of the plane based on a 2-adic valuation on $\mathbb{R}$ together with Sperner's lemma. Subsequent work established similar results for regular polygons, centrally symmetric polygons, and polyominoes. In 2000, Stein proposed a common generalisation of the centrally symmetric and polyomino cases to balanced polygons. In 2014, Rudenko introduced a new perspective on the problem and proved Stein's conjecture for dissections with rational vertex coordinates. Building on and streamlining his approach, we resolve the conjecture in full.

title: Ramsey sets are canonically Ramsey
summary: A set $A$ of points is called Ramsey if, for each $r$, every $r$-coloring of a sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $A$. We show that for each Ramsey set $A$, every $r$-coloring of a sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space, regardless of the number of colors used, contains a monochromatic or a rainbow congruent copy of $A$. This answers a question raised in virtually every paper on the topic.

title: Structural properties of semi-cutting sets
summary: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple undirected graph, let $T\subseteq V$, and let $F\subseteq E$. We call $F$ semi-cutting for $T$ if $d_{G}(u,w)<d_{G\setminus F}(u,w)$ for every two distinct terminals $u,w\in T$. We prove the sharp bound $|F|\ge |T|-1$. The argument is structural: semi-cutting sets are first identified with edge transversals of all shortest terminal-terminal paths, and the bound then follows from a contraction step, a terminal-deletion lemma, and a lexicographic induction on $(|T|,|V|)$.

title: Canonical activation patterns and ReLU pattern varieties
summary: A ReLU pattern variety records the polynomial relations among the coefficients of the affine maps associated with a prescribed set of activation patterns of a ReLU network. We study how the combinatorics of the canonical set of activation patterns of an unbiased ReLU network is reflected in the geometry of its pattern variety. In particular, we introduce the notion of pattern stability and characterize pattern stability and combinatorial stability for shallow networks. When the associated wall graph is connected and contains an edge of every neuron label, we resolve a problem of Alexandr and Montúfar by determining the defining ideal of the associated pattern variety explicitly. We establish a hierarchy of progressively weaker equivalence relations relating labeled combinatorial equivalence, equality and permutation equivalence of canonical pattern sets, and equivalences of the associated varieties. Finally, we relate functional dimension to the differential of the pattern map and show that it is bounded above by the dimension of the canonical pattern variety at every depth. For nondegenerate shallow networks, we give an exact formula for the functional dimension; for every shallow architecture, it equals the dimension of the canonical pattern variety on an open dense set of full Lebesgue measure.

title: Equilateral-triangle-free sets in finite planes
summary: For a prime $p>3$, let $F(p)$ be the largest cardinality of a subset of $\mathbb F_p^2$ containing no equilateral triangle with nonzero squared side length. Alex Iosevich asked for the exact value of $F(p)$. By constructing such subsets of $\mathbb F_p^2$ from cap sets in $\mathbb F_3^n$, we obtain the uniform lower bounds \[ F(p)\gg \begin{cases} p^{2γ}, & p\equiv 11\pmod{12},\\ p^{1+γ}, & p\equiv 1\pmod{12}. \end{cases} \] Here $γ=\log_3(2.2202)$, so the two exponents are $1.452008666\ldots$ and $1.726004333\ldots$, respectively. We also apply a quantitative corners theorem to show that $F(p)=o(p^2)$ as $p\to\infty$ through either congruence class.

title: A proof of a conjecture on bipartite correspondence packing
summary: A correspondence cover assigns a set of possible colors to each vertex of a graph. For each edge, a matching between the two endpoint color sets specifies the forbidden color pairs. A correspondence coloring selects one color at each vertex so that no forbidden pair is selected. A full correspondence packing is a collection of such colorings that uses every color at each vertex exactly once. We prove a conjecture of Cambie, Cames van Batenburg, Davies, and Kang [Random Structures & Algorithms 64 (2024), 62--93]. For every sufficiently large $D$, there is a positive integer $k(D)=(1+o(1))D/\log D$ such that every correspondence cover of any finite bipartite graph has a full correspondence packing if each color has at most $D$ forbidden partners and each vertex has $k(D)$ colors. More precisely, we prove this conclusion with \[ k(D)=\left\lceil\frac{D}{\log D-2\log\log D-6}\right\rceil \] for every integer $D\ge\lceil e^{20}\rceil$.

title: Graph Intersections and Hypergraph Discrepancy
summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs on $n$ vertices with $e(G)=p\binom{n}{2}$ and $e(H)=q\binom{n}{2}$, where $p,q\in(0,1)$ are fixed. Bollobás and Scott studied intersections of two graphs under random relabelling and asked for the minimum $L^2$ norm of the deviation of their intersection size from its expected value. We answer this question by proving that, for graphs of order $n$ with fixed edge densities $p,q\in(0,1)$, the minimum is \begin{equation*} \left(\sqrt{\frac{p(1-p)q(1-q)}{2}\cdot\frac{1-\sqrt R}{1+\sqrt R}}\right)n+o(n), \end{equation*} where $R=\max\{p,1-p,q,1-q\}$. The coefficient of the linear term is best possible. Bollobás and Scott defined the positive and negative discrepancies of two hypergraphs as the largest deviations of their intersection size above and below its expected value under relabelling, respectively. They asked for the minimum product of the positive and negative discrepancies of two $(n/2)$-uniform hypergraphs on $n$ vertices with $\frac{1}{2}\binom{n}{n/2}$ edges. We answer this question by proving that the minimum product of these discrepancies is $0$ if $4\mid\binom{n}{n/2}$ and $1/4$ otherwise.

title: $L$-systems on the large Witt design
summary: Let $L=\{0,1,2,3,4,8\}$, associated with the large Witt design $S(5,8,24)$, and let $m(n,24,L)$ be the maximum size of a family of $24$-element subsets of an $n$-element set whose distinct members have intersection sizes in $L$. We prove that there are positive constants $c,C,n_0$ such that, for every $n\geq n_0$, \[ cn^{316/63}\leq m(n,24,L)\leq Cn^{169/29}. \] We also obtain similar results for the systems associated with $S(4,7,23)$, $S(3,6,22)$, and $S(3,4,14)$. The upper bounds follow from a non-Shannon information inequality and disprove conjectures of Kupavskii and Terekhov. The lower bounds follow from an algebraic construction for arbitrary Steiner systems.

title: Treewidth and Separation Number: An Optimal Linear Bound
summary: The \emph{separation number} $\sn(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the smallest integer $a$ such that every subgraph $H$ of $G$ admits a separation $(A,B)$ of {\em order} $|A\cap B|\le a$ whose two sides $A\setminus B$ and $B\setminus A$ each contain at most $2|V(H)|/3$ vertices. Dvořák and Norin proved that $\tw(G)\le 15\sn(G)$ for every nonempty graph $G$. We improve the constant to its optimal value: every nonempty graph satisfies $\tw(G)\le 4\sn(G)-2$. This is best possible: for every $k\ge 2$, there is a graph $G_k$ with $\tw(G_k)=4k+2$ and $\sn(G_k)=k+1$.

title: On homogeneous hypertournaments
summary: Sullivan recently constructed continuum many countable homogeneous $n$-hypertournaments for every $n\ge3$ by forbidding configurations he calls pair-cancelling. We show that, for every family $\mathcal F$ of pair-cancelling $n$-hypertournaments, the class of all linearly ordered finite $\mathcal F$-free $n$-hypertournaments is Ramsey and has the ordering property. In particular, freely ordered $\mathbf{H}_4$-free $3$-hypertournaments are Ramsey, answering a question of Cherlin, Hubička, Nešetřil, and the author from 2021. For every odd $n\ge3$, we give a simple Ramsey expansion with the expansion property for even $n$-hypertournaments by naming an $(n-1)$-hypertournament and a free linear order. We also show that, for $n\ge6$, no unbounded hereditary strong amalgamation class of finite $n$-hypertournaments has EPPA. Moreover, we prove the failure of EPPA for all Sullivan's classes with $n\ge4$, and for the even $5$-hypertournaments. We conjecture that even hypertournaments and classes omitting a family of pair-cancelling hypertournaments, together with the homogeneous cyclic order in arity three, are the only countably infinite homogeneous $n$-hypertournaments for $n\ge3$. We give some supporting evidence.

title: Collapsibility of Vietoris--Rips complexes of hypercube graphs in codimension two
summary: Shukla conjectured that the collapsibility number of the Vietoris-Rips complex $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ of the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph at scale $r$ equals $2^r$ for all $n\ge r+1$. We prove the conjecture for $n=r+2$ and every $r$, which gives the first known cases with $r\ge 4$ beyond the cross-polytope case $n=r+1$. Writing $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ as the independence complex of the graph $H_{n,r}$ that joins two points when their Hamming distance exceeds $r$, we construct a cover of $H_{r+2,r}$ by $2^r$ co-chordal subgraphs. The key general tool is the inequality that, for every graph $G$, the $θ$-number of Bıyıkoğlu and Civan of the independence complex of $G$, and hence the collapsibility number of that complex, is at most the co-chordal cover number of $G$; this strengthens Woodroofe's regularity bound. We also show, using a theorem of Alon, Jin, and Sudakov, that the induced matching number of $H_{n,r}$ equals $2^r$ for every $n>r$, and that $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ is vertex decomposable if and only if $r=1$ or $n=r+1$. As consequences, we determine the top degree of nonvanishing homology and the coconnectivity of $\mathrm{VR}(I_{r+2};r)$, and we prove split injectivity in top-degree integral homology. Finally, assuming a recent skew Hamming set-pair theorem of Gao and Zhao, we prove that the collapsibility number of $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ is at most $2^{r+1}-4$ for all $n>r\ge 2$.

title: Creation Sequences for Numerical Semigroups and Exact Counts of Semigroup Partitions
summary: A numerical semigroup is a subset of the non-negative integers that contains $0$, is closed under addition and has finite complement. A threshold graph is built by adding vertices one at a time, each new vertex being isolated or dominating, and the record of these choices is its \emph{creation sequence}. Reading the creation sequence as a lattice path gives an integer partition and, through the Keith--Nath correspondence, a numerical set in which the dominating vertices are the elements and the isolated vertices are the gaps. We show that threshold graphs with an isolated vertex correspond bijectively to numerical sets, and we study numerical semigroups through their creation sequences. We prove that in the creation sequence of a numerical semigroup of multiplicity $m$ every block of ones and every non-initial block of zeros has length less than $m$, we give criteria for partitions with a unique smallest part and with two distinct part sizes, and we classify all partitions with at most four parts. We show that every partition $λ$ with $g$ parts corresponding to a numerical semigroup satisfies $\ell(λ)\geλ_1$ and, more strongly, fits inside the staircase $(g,g-1,\dots,1)$; equivalently, its creation sequence begins with a Dyck path. Its size equals the genus plus the Weierstrass weight of the semigroup, and asymptotically at most half of all partitions correspond to numerical semigroups. Finally, we obtain exact formulas for the numbers of partitions of $n$ corresponding to numerical semigroups of genus $g$, multiplicity $m$ and Frobenius number $f$, valid in the sharp ranges $g\ge n/2$, $m>n/3$ and $f\ge n-\frac{n-1}{4}$. These formulas solve the open problems posed by Burson, Nam and Sisneros-Thiry \cite{BNS}, recover all of their counting theorems, and correct several of their statements.

title: Characterization of Cubic Graphs with Exactly Two Lonely Edges
summary: Perfect matchings are fundamental to understanding structural connectivity in cubic graphs, with "lonely edges" (edges in exactly one perfect matching) forming a critical underexplored class. Goedgebeur et al. (J. Graph Theory, 112 (2026) 276-289) established an upper bound of 6 on the number of lonely edges in 3-connected non-double covered cubic graphs and completely characterized the classes $\mathcal{U}_k$ for $3 \le k \le 6$. Narayana et al. subsequently gave a recursive characterization of the subclass in which the two lonely edges lie in the same perfect matching. This paper completes the classification by presenting a full structural characterization of $\mathcal{U}_2$, the family of 3-connected cubic graphs with exactly two lonely edges. We identify the minimally non-contractible "primitive kernels" of $\mathcal{U}_2$ and develop constructive operations to generate any graph in $\mathcal{U}_2$ from these kernels.

title: Linear Algebra over Bands
summary: We introduce Eckmann-Hilton operators on bands, which allow for a suite of matroidal constructions, in particular, matroid unions and matroid stable intersections. This enables the construction of general linear monoids over bands. Geometrically, we show that matroid stable intersection extends the transverse intersection of linear spaces over fields and the stable intersection of tropical linear spaces, lending new insight into intersection theory on bands.
