title: List colouring of circular-arc graphs
summary: A circular-arc graph takes a set of nonempty closed arcs on a circle as its vertex set, and two vertices are adjacent when their corresponding arcs intersect on the circle. We show the chromatic number of any circular-arc graph equals its list chromatic number. Our methodology is an application of Schauz's coefficient formula within the Alon-Tarsi and Combinatorial Nullstellensatz framework.

title: Triples in matroid circuits
summary: We prove that, if $X$ is a four-element independent set in a vertically $5$-connected representable matroid $M$, then either there is a circuit of $M$ that contains at least three elements of $X$, or there is a representation $A$ of $M$ such that each column of $A$ has at most two non-zero elements and each of the columns indexed by $X$ has exactly one non-zero element. We also prove a version of this result without the connectivity assumptions.

title: Projective planes with abelian collineation groups of type (F) are Desarguesian
summary: We use prime ideal factorization and residue class fields of cyclotomic integer rings to prove that every abelian direct product difference set is classical. This implies that every projective plane of order $n$ with an abelian collineation group of order $n(n-1)$ is Desarguesian, proving a conjecture of Jungnickel and de Resmini. As a consequence, we obtain the classification of circular Costas maps and of Costas polynomials conjectured by Muratovic-Ribic, Pott, Thomson and Wang and by Torres and Rubio.

title: Symmetric Chemical Reaction Networks: Realizations and Steady States
summary: We investigate symmetric chemical reaction networks and their steady states. From classical equivariant dynamical systems and network theory it is known that the mass- action ODE of any symmetric chemical reaction network is equivariant. For symmetries that permute the species, we prove that any equivariant mass-action ODE is realized by a symmetric chemical reaction network and construct a sparsest such realization. We apply the half-degree principle to show that a symmetric CRN that has a steady state also has one with few distinct coordinates.

title: Odd faces as a parameter for maximum independent set in embedded graphs
summary: We give a polynomial-time algorithm for finding a maximum weight independent set in a graph embedded in a surface of bounded genus and with a bounded number of vertex-disjoint odd faces. In particular, we obtain an algorithm for graphs with an even-faced embedding in a torus and for planar graphs with a bounded number of odd faces, answering a question of Thomassé (2018) and a question of Choi, Gorsky, Kim, McFarland, and Wiederrecht (2025) respectively. We reduce the original problem to finding a minimum cost non-negative integer circulation with homology constraints in the dual of a certain double cover of the original graph.

title: Arithmetic Universality and Integer Decomposition in Disjunctions of Three Staircase Simplices
summary: The staircase simplices $\{x\in[0,1]^d:x_{σ(1)}\le\cdots\le x_{σ(d)}\}$, $σ\in S_d\,$, are the $d!$ unimodular cells of the staircase triangulation of the unit cube. The disjunctive hull (Cayley polytope) of a selection $P_0, \ldots, P_n$ of them has the integer decomposition property (IDP) if, for all integers $λ_i\ge0$, every lattice point of $\sum_iλ_i P_i$ is a sum of vertices, $λ_i$ of them from $P_i$. For two simplices, IDP always holds. For three, every nontrivial finite abelian group $G$ arises, in the optimal dimension $Θ(\log|G|)$, as the residue group of a simplex facet whose $|G|-1$ nonzero box points are Hilbert basis elements of the whole cone; $k$ times such a point is a sum of vertices exactly when its order in $G$ divides $k$. Isolating this arithmetic is costly: if a simplex face has a single Hilbert basis element $h$ that is not a vertex, then $kh$ is a sum of vertices exactly when some $q$ divides $k$, and $d\ge3q-2$, attained for every $q\ge3$; we also find the least dimension for each $G$ with the fewest such elements. Without isolation, every nonzero submonoid of $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ omitting $1$ is $\{k\ge0:kh$ is a sum of vertices$\}$ for a Hilbert basis element $h$ of degree three. For every $0/1$ polytope with $N$ vertices in $\mathbb{R}^r$, three staircase simplices in dimension $O(N(r+1))$ have a face that has IDP exactly when the polytope does. Deciding whether a lattice point $h$ is a sum of vertices is strongly NP-complete, even given vertex expressions of $2h$ and $3h$, and recognizing IDP of a designated facet is coNP-complete; for the whole hull, IDP can first fail in degree linear in $d$, and it holds whenever $d\le5$. For a family of triples defined by words over three letters, we determine the entire Hilbert basis and characterize IDP by two forbidden subsequences.

title: \(A_α\)-Wronskian Vertices of Paths and Controllability of Path-Rooted Products
summary: For a graph \(G\) with adjacency and degree matrices \(A(G)\) and \(D(G)\), set \(A_α(G)=αD(G)+(1-α)A(G)\) for \(0\leqα<1\). Using Chebyshev polynomials and a theorem of Conway and Jones, we classify the \(A_α\)-Wronskian vertices of every path \(P_n\), \(n\geq2\) (equivalently, the standard basis vectors cyclic for \(A_α(P_n)\)). The central vertex of an odd-order path is never Wronskian; for every other vertex, we determine an explicit finite set of algebraic exceptional parameters. These sets contain no rational parameters other than \(0\) and \(1/2\), for which the adjacency and signless Laplacian cases are characterized by gcd criteria. For even-order paths rooted at either central vertex, we explicitly evaluate the root resultant and the walk-determinant polynomial in the rooted-product factorization. The resulting controllability criterion combines \(A_α\)-controllability of the base graph with at most three explicit spectral exclusions. For each parameter, one of two fixed complementary base graphs yields controllable products for every even-order path and both central roots. For \(1/2\leqα<1\), algebraic conjugates further simplify the spectral test for general rooted products.

title: Polynomial bounds for quasiplanar graphs
summary: A graph $G$ is $k$-quasiplanar if it can be drawn in the plane without $k$ pairwise crossing edges. It was a longstanding conjecture that $n$-vertex $k$-quasiplanar graphs have $O_k(n)$ edges. This was recently resolved by Sadhu and, independently, by Pach, Tardos, and Zeng, based on a theorem in topology proven by Beeker and Lazarovich. These papers showed that $k$-quasiplanar graphs have at most $k^{O(k)}n$ edges. In this note, we greatly improve the dependence on $k$ and show that every $k$-quasiplanar $n$-vertex graph has at most $O(k^2n)$ edges. The proof is based on a geometric charging scheme and Erdős-Szekeres type combinatorial arguments.

title: Perfect 3-colorings of the generalized Petersen graphs GP(n,2)
summary: We enumerate the parameter matrices of all perfect 3-colorings of the generalized Petersen graphs GP(n,2), n >= 5. We show that there are only five matrices that can be the parameter matrix of such a coloring. Two of them occur if and only if 5 | n, two occur if and only if 3 | n, and the remaining one occurs if and only if 10 | n.

title: Counting Matrices of Prescribed Jordan Type in Incidence Algebras
summary: We count nilpotent matrices in the incidence algebra of a finite poset over a finite field that belong to a prescribed conjugacy class for the adjoint action of the general linear group. We prove that these counts depend only on the comparability graph of the poset. We introduce shuffle-prefix posets, a class containing all finite interval orders, and give explicit formulas for their nilpotent Jordan counts. These counts are polynomials with integer coefficients in the field size, valid over every finite field. Finally, Fourier duality relates conjugacy-class counts in a coordinate subspace to those in the subspace supported on the complementary matrix positions, whenever one subspace consists entirely of nilpotent matrices.

title: Crossing Numbers of Complete Graphs: the independent odd crossing number
summary: We show that the Harary--Hill bound on the crossing number of complete graphs as well as the Zarankiewwicz bound on the crossing number of complete bipartite graphs, both recently established by OpenAI, also hold for the independent odd crossing number. This implies that the same bounds hold for several other crossing number variants such as the (independent) algebraic crossing number and the (independent) pair crossing number.

title: Regular subgroups of wreath products and Cayley Cartesian products
summary: The Cartesian product of Cayley graphs is again a Cayley graph. For connected graphs, the converse question reduces to Cartesian powers of Cartesian-prime graphs, and consequently to the study of regular subgroups of wreath products in the product action. We prove that, for a transitive permutation group $G$ of degree $2p$ or $4p$, where $p$ is prime, $G\wr S_2$ contains a regular subgroup if and only if $G$ does, and construct counterexamples of degree $8p$ for every prime $p\equiv3\pmod4$. By modifying this construction, we obtain an infinite family of connected non-Cayley graphs whose Cartesian squares are Cayley graphs, giving a negative answer to the converse question. The smallest graph in our family has $120$ vertices and valency $27$. In contrast, we prove that a connected vertex-transitive graph of order $pq$, where $p$ and $q$ are primes, has a Cayley Cartesian power if and only if the graph itself is Cayley.

title: Peak state transfer in trees and the cost of distance
summary: There is peak state transfer between vertices $u$ and $v$ in a graph $G$ if there exists a time $t$ for which $|(\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm i t M})_{u,v}|$ saturates the triangle inequality imposed by its spectral decomposition and $M$ is either the adjacency or Laplacian matrix. We show that peak state transfer at distance $d$ requires $\frac{d^3}{24}(1 + o(1))$ edges in the adjacency case, $Ω(d^2)$ edges in the Laplacian case, and that the leading coefficient in the former is tight. We find a family of graphs with Laplacian peak state transfer at distance $d$ and $Θ(d^5)$ edges, showing that peak state transfer is achievable in a polynomial graph size. In contrast, Laplacian perfect state transfer costs at least $Ω(2^{d/2})$ edges when the distance partition of vertices around one vertex is almost equitable. Finally, we show that Laplacian peak state transfer in trees requires $Ω(d!)$ edges, and we characterize all trees of diameter $\leq 4$ admitting Laplacian peak state transfer, thus answering a pair of questions posed by Coutinho, Guo, and Schmeits.

title: Landau's problems through ratios of $L$-functions
summary: Very recently, Lee announced a proof of the Twin Prime Conjecture assuming the Ratios Conjecture for the Riemann zeta function. We obtain conditional asymptotic formulas with power-saving errors for each of Landau's four prime problems. In the function field setting, using Sawin's estimates for factorization functions in squarefree progressions and a discriminant cohomology argument, we obtain unconditional Goldbach and prime-pair asymptotics over sufficiently large fixed odd fields, including prime fields. Similar results may be possible for other problems in analytic number theory.

title: Irreducible Projective Polynomials
summary: Suppose $q=p^{s_1}$ and $σ=p^{s_2}$ for a prime $p$ and $s_1,s_2\in\mathbb{N}.$ In this paper, we characterize for which values of $p, d, s_1, s_2, \ell$ there exists an irreducible polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of the form \begin{align*} x^\frac{σ^d-1}{\ell}+\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}a_j x^\frac{σ^j-1}{\ell} \end{align*} for fixed $d,\ell\in\mathbb{N}$ where $\ell\mid (σ-1).$ In particular, we enumerate irreducible polynomials of this form.

title: On p-adic modularity of abelian threefolds with imaginary multiplication and rational p-isogeny
summary: We prove $p$-adic modularity of a certain class of abelian threefolds over $\mathbf{Q}$ (with imaginary multiplication and rational $p$-isogeny), including the Jacobians of some genus 3 curves known as Picard curves. More precisely, we study a deformation problem for residual 3-dimensional totally reducible Galois pseudorepresentations over an imaginary quadratic field which are ordinary at primes over $p$ and conjugate self-dual. We show that under certain conditions the universal pseudodeformation ring in any weight (including the non-classical low weight corresponding to an abelian threefold) is isomorphic to a specialization of the ordinary Hida Hecke algebra on $U(2,1)$. The conditions that we assume are essentially class group conditions as well as weak regularity of the Hecke algebras in sufficiently high classical weights.

title: The first-order theory of the ring of integers of any abelian extension of $\Q$ is undecidable
summary: We show that any ring of totally real abelian integers has a JR-number and therefore the first-order theory of every ring of totally real abelian integers is undecidable. It then follows that the first-order theory of the ring of integers of any abelian extension of $\Q$ is undecidable and that there is one formula without parameters defining $\Z$ in any such ring. The main arithmetic input is a recent paper of Bajpai, Das, Kedlaya, and Mello proving that the houses of cyclotomic integers form a well-ordered subset of $\R$.

title: An ancient diophantine problem of Brahmagupta
summary: In the seventh century CE, Brahmagupta gave a parametric solution to the problem of finding two numbers $x$ and $y$ such that $x+y, x-y$ and $xy+1$ are all squares. We describe a method for generating infinitely many rational parametric solutions of the problem and another method for generating parametric solutions of the problem in terms of univariate polynomials with integer coefficients. The complete solution of the problem still remains elusive.

title: Two-Sided large oscillations of the argument of the Riemann zeta function and its iterates
summary: Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we establish lower bounds for large oscillations of the iterated argument functions \(S_n(t)\) of the Riemann zeta function. As a corollary, we prove that, for every fixed integer \(n \geq 0\), \[S_n(t)=Ω_{\pm}\Big(\frac{(\log t)^{1/2}(\log_3 t)^{1/2}}{(\log_2 t)^{n+1/2}} \Big).\] For even \(n\), this recovers two results of Chirre and Mahatab in 2021. For odd \(n\), our result strengthens theirs by establishing the missing direction of oscillation with the same order of magnitude.

title: An Explicit Version of Serre's Open Image Theorem for Galois Number Fields
summary: In 1971, Serre showed that the mod $p$ Galois representation associated to a non-CM elliptic curve over a number field is surjective for all but finitely many primes $p$. That is, there exists a constant $c(E,K)$, for $E$ a non-CM elliptic curve over a number field $K$, such that $ρ_{E,p}:\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)\to \mathrm{Aut}(E[p])$ is surjective for all primes $p>c(E,K)$. We give a bound for this constant using an effective version of the Faltings isogeny theorem for specific number fields. We show that, for $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{D})$ with $|D|<50$ and $K$ a formally real number field, given a non-CM elliptic curve $E$ over $K$ we have $c(E,K)\le 2C_1(K)\log N_{K/\mathbb Q}\operatorname{rad}\left( 2\mathcal O_K\mathfrak N_{E}\right )+2 C_2(K)$, where $\mathfrak N_E$ denotes the conductor ideal of $E$, and the constants $C_1(K)$ and $C_2(K)$ can be described explicitly. We also show that for primes greater than this bound, the image cannot be contained in the normalizer of a non-split Cartan subgroup. This works for any Galois number field. Our proof assumes the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH).

title: On the number of elite primes
summary: A prime $p$ is elite if all sufficiently large Fermat numbers $F_n=2^{2^n}+1$ are quadratic nonresidues modulo $p$. Let $E(x)$ be the number of elite primes up to $x$. The best published bounds are $E(x)\ll x/(\log x)^{3/2}$ unconditionally and $E(x)\ll x^{5/6}$ under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), both due to Just. Just and Pollack remarked, without a written proof, that sorting primes by the exact power of $2$ dividing $p-1$ should give $x/(\log x)^{2-\varepsilon}$ and $x^{3/4+\varepsilon}$. We give complete proofs of slightly sharper statements: $E(x)\le(16+o(1))x\log\log x/(\log x)^2$ unconditionally, and $E(x)\ll x^{3/4}(\log x)^{1/2}$ under GRH. We also recall, with short proofs, known facts about the period of $(F_n\bmod p)$ that go back to Aigner: every elite prime $p$ satisfies the defining condition from the index $v_2(\operatorname{ord}_p 2)$ onwards, and the period is even unless $p\in\{3,5\}$. Finally, we show under GRH that, when the moduli involved are at most $x^{1/3}$, the set of primes bounded by the sieve argument has size $\asymp x\log\log x/(\log x)^2$. This indicates that the remaining factor $\log\log x$ cannot be removed by this method alone. All theorems of the paper have been formalized in the Lean 4 proof assistant, with the Brun--Titchmarsh inequality and two standard consequences of GRH as explicit hypotheses.
comment: 11 pages. Includes a Lean 4 formalization with three analytic inputs as explicit hypotheses

title: Counting integral points of fixed degree and given height over function fields
summary: Let $k$ be a finite extension of the rational function field in one variable over a finite field, and let $\mathcal{O}_k$ be its ring of integers. Let $\overline{k}$ be an algebraic closure of $k$. For integers $e \geq 2$ and $n \geq 1$, we study the number of points in the affine space $\overline{k}^n$ whose coordinates are integral over $\mathcal{O}_k$, have absolute logarithmic Weil height equal to $m \geq 0$, and generate an extension of degree $e$ over $k$. More precisely, we derive an asymptotic formula for this quantity as $m \rightarrow \infty$ whenever $n > e$, except in the cases $(n,e)\in \{(3,2),(4,3),(5,4)\}$. When $k$ is the rational function field, however, we use Weierstrass semigroups to obtain asymptotic formulas for the cases $(n,e)\in \{(1,2),(2,2),(3,2)\}$, thereby completing the picture in the setting $e=2$. As an application, we also derive asymptotic estimates for the number of certain decomposable forms with coefficients in $\mathcal{O}_k$.

title: Two Quintic Diophantine Equations and Fifth Powers in Fibonacci Sums at Distance Five
summary: Let $F_n$ denote the $n$th Fibonacci number. We study the Diophantine equation $$ F_{n+5}+F_n=y^5 $$ in positive integers $n$ and $y$. We prove that this equation has no solutions. The proof uses a recurrence identity to reduce the problem to the two equations $$ X^2-5Z^5=44,\qquad X^2+44=5Z^5. $$ We show that the first equation has exactly the solutions $(X,Z)=(\pm7,1)$ for $Z>0$, and that the second has no such solutions. To obtain these results, we use ideal factorization in $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{11})$ and $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-11})$ and reduce the problem to six quintic Thue equations. Their complete solution sets are computed with the Magma Online Calculator and independently verified with PARI/GP.

title: Weighted unit equations in cyclic cubic orders
summary: We study nonrational integral units $u,v$ satisfying $au+sv=1$, with integers $1<a<s$, in varying cyclic cubic fields. The ratio $u/v$ generates the joint order $R=\mathbb{Z}[u,v]$ and gives effective finiteness for each fixed first weight and each fixed gap. Consecutive weights yield exactly seven simultaneous-isomorphism classes, at $a=2,4,13$; in every proper order among them, $\{-1,u,v\}$ generates $R^\times$.

title: Test of p-rationality of a number field--pari/gp programs
summary: We give a new computational approach of p-rationality of a number field k, when the method using ray class groups is out of reach in a reasonable time when the degree of k and p are too large. The method is based for a part on the utilisation of the Logp-function that we have defined in the 80's. The general pari/gp program makes no assumptions about k and p. For quadratic fields, we give other programs giving more information (surprisingly these programs, with many instructions, are much faster).
comment: The programs may be copied and pasted, on tex or pdf files, without any knowledge of PARI language. They have been tested as much as possible. They give the response (k is or not p-rational) whatever k and p. Any comments and remarks for improvements are welcome

title: The Estermann Problem with Almost Proportional Summands
summary: We obtain a family of estimates for short Weyl sums $$ \left| \sum_{x-y<m\le x}e^{2πiαm^n} \right| \ll y\left( \frac{1}{q}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{q}{y^n} \right)^{\frac{s-1}{s\cdot2^{n-1}}} \bigl(\log(qy)\bigr)^{ \frac{(n-1)^s+s-2}{s\cdot2^{n-1}}}, $$ where $n\ge3$ and $s\ge2$ are fixed integers, $x\ge y\ge2$, $α\in\mathbb R$, $a\in\mathbb Z$, $q\in\mathbb N$, $(a,q)=1$, and $\left|α-\frac{a}{q}\right|\le\frac{1}{q^2}$. For $n\ge4$, we also derive from the modern form of Vinogradov's mean value theorem the estimate $$ \left| \sum_{x-y<m\le x}e^{2πiαm^n} \right| \ll y\left( \frac{1}{q}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{q}{y^n} \right)^{\frac{1}{n(n-1)+2}} \log y. $$ Using these estimates, repeated Dirichlet approximation, and an estimate in the intermediate range, we establish an asymptotic formula for the number of representations $$ p_1+p_2+m^n=N,\quad |p_i-μ_iN|\le H,\quad i=1,2, \quad |m^n-μ_3N|\le H, $$ where $p_1,p_2$ are primes, $m$ is a positive integer, and $μ_1,μ_2,μ_3$ are fixed positive numbers whose sum is $1$. The asymptotic formula holds in the range $$ N^{1-θ_n}(\log N)^{A_n}\le H\le N^{1-δ}, \qquad θ_n=\min\left\{\frac{1}{2n},\frac{2}{n^2}\right\}, $$ where $0<δ<θ_n$ is fixed, $A_3=3$, $A_4=\frac{61}{4}$, and $A_n=6n-12+\frac{22}{n}-\frac{12}{n^2}$ for $n\ge5$. In the cubic case, the logarithmic exponent in the previously known lower bound for $H$ is reduced from $10$ to $3$. For $n\ge4$, the exponent of $N$ is reduced from $1-\frac{1}{n(n-1)}$ to $1-\frac{2}{n^2}$.

title: Joint quadratic base changes of elliptic surfaces with torsion Z/4Z and Z/2Z x Z/6Z
summary: We study elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ obtained from an elliptic surface by imposing two quadratic conditions, each of which produces a new point. By the Kani-Rosen decomposition, the joint cover is rational only when the branch loci of the two conditions meet; for two quadratic conditions this means that they share a root. We apply this to two surfaces. For Elkies's rank-four K3 surface with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$, a catalogue of $194$ quadratic conditions contains exactly two such pairs. One recovers the rank-six curve of the authors; the other gives a second, inequivalent curve with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$ and rank six. For the universal curve with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z}$, $42$ conditions give exactly $21$ rational joint covers, which yield seven curves of rank two. Two more arise from a tower of conditions. Five of these nine curves are the curves of Dujella, Kazalicki and Peral; the other four are not equivalent to any of them. In both cases we determine the Mordell-Weil groups over $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ exactly, and we prove that the curves are pairwise inequivalent under invertible changes of parameter, even over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$.

title: The monogenicity of $\boldsymbol{x^n+c\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}a^{n-j-1}x^j}$
summary: We say that a monic polynomial $f(x)\in {\mathbb Z}[x]$ is {\em monogenic} if $f(x)$ is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$ and $\{1,θ,θ^2,\ldots,θ^{{\rm deg}(f)-1}\}$ is a basis for the ring of integers of ${\mathbb Q}(θ)$, where $f(θ)=0$. Let $n,a,c\in {\mathbb Z}$ with $n\ge 3$, and suppose that \[{\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x):=x^n+cx^{n-1}+acx^{n-2}+a^2cx^{n-3}+\cdots +a^{n-2}cx+a^{n-1}c\] is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$. Recently, Jakhar, Kalwaniya and Yadav have given necessary and sufficient conditions for the monogenicity of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$, under the assumption that all prime divisors of the discriminant of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$ not dividing $ac$ also do not divide $n+1$. In this note, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the monogenicity of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$ without this restriction.

title: Pair Correlation Conjecture for the Zeros of Artin $L$-functions I: Simple and Critical Zeros
summary: In 1973, Montgomery posed the pair correlation conjecture (PCC) for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Motivated by PCC, Montgomery conjectured that the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function are almost surely simple, and proved that at least $2/3$ are simple assuming the Riemann hypothesis (RH). In 1978, Mueller and Gallagher were able to prove asymptotically $100\%$ are simple assuming PCC and RH. Recently, Goldston et al. noticed that the assumption of RH can be removed in Mueller and Gallagher's method. In fact, assuming PCC by itself without RH is sufficient to prove that asymptotically $100\%$ of the nontrivial zeros are both simple and on the critical line. We adapt the notion of horizontal multiplicity from Goldston et al. to show that the nontrivial zeros of Artin $L$-functions attached to irreducible linear representation of the Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$ are almost surely simple and lie on the critical line without assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH). We will assume the appropriate version of PCC along with some other widely believed conjectures.

title: Khinchin's constant along deterministic subsequences
summary: Khinchin's theorem says that, for Lebesgue almost every real number, the geometric mean of the partial quotients in its continued fraction expansion converges to a universal constant $K\approx 2.6854520010\ldots$. We show that the same constant is obtained when the partial quotients are sampled along any fixed strictly increasing deterministic sequence of indices. Thus arithmetic progressions, polynomial sequences, prime indices, and lacunary sequences all give the usual Khinchin constant. We also look at a different selection rule: instead of restricting the indices, we restrict the values of the partial quotients. In this case the answer changes. The geometric mean of the prime-valued partial quotients converges almost surely to a new constant $K_{\mathcal P}\approx {3.439477971}\ldots$.

title: ECPack.wl: A Mathematica Package for Elliptic Curves over the Rationals and Finite Fields
summary: We present a Mathematica package entitled ECPack.wl, where we implement many important properties and commands relevant to the study of elliptic curves over the rationals and finite fields, namely $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{F}_q$, where $q=p^r$ and $p$ is prime. By streamlining the analysis of general elliptic curves and their transformations, ECPack.wl offers foundational computational tools for applications in high-energy physics, including elliptic Feynman integrals. This package significantly extends the functionalities of a package due to McGee in so far as we are able to study all versions of elliptic curves, such as the long Weierstrass, quartic and Legendre forms. We implement suitable transformations that are required for the general case, as well as those associated with fields of characteristic 2 and 3. Furthermore, the package computes many curve properties, such as point arithmetic, minimality checks, rank bounds and analytic rank, group structure, invariants, and the Weil and Tate pairings, over both $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{F}_p$, as well as the Kodaira classification of the singular fibres of one-parameter families of elliptic curves, with the associated F-theory data. The package and its accompanying notebooks are available at https://github.com/DhamakedarDarsh/Mathematica-Code-and-worked-out-notebooks-for-Elliptic-Curves

title: Distribution of Primes in Galois Extensions of Global Fields with Explicit Constant Terms
summary: We study the distribution of primes among Frobenius conjugacy classes in finite Galois extensions of global fields. In earlier work, the author and Koyama proved that the existence and nonvanishing of the limit of partial Euler products on the critical line for Artin $L$-functions (the Deep Riemann Hypothesis (A), or DRH(A)) are equivalent to an asymptotic formula for weighted prime counting functions with an unspecified constant term. In this article, we prove that a refined asymptotic formula is equivalent to the full version of DRH, namely the convergence of the Euler products on the critical line (DRH(A)) and the determination of their limiting values (DRH(B)). Here, the constant term is given explicitly in terms of the residue of the zeta function, central derivatives of Artin $L$-functions, ramified primes, and higher prime-power contributions.

title: On Primitive Divisor Multiplicities of Lucas Sequences
summary: Let $(U_{n})$ be a nondegenerate Lucas sequence with coprime integer parameters. Assuming the rational $abc$ conjecture, we prove that almost every index $n$ has a primitive prime divisor of $U_{n}$ of multiplicity one. More quantitatively, the logarithmic contribution of repeated primitive prime factors tends to zero relative to the primitive part along any family with $φ(n) / n$ bounded below, and also in Cesàro mean over all indices. We derive explicit logarithmic lower bounds for Lucas non-Wieferich primes with ranks in prescribed residue classes. Both signs of the discriminant are allowed. Independently, we describe initial multiplicities at good odd primes by a unique Hensel root in the recurrence-parameter disk and by the exact contraction rate of a normalized Dickson-polynomial iteration. Applications include rank and period lifting for Fibonacci numbers and the Wall-Sun-Sun condition.

title: On the behavior of the number of $k$-full integers between successive $k$-th powers
summary: Let $k\ge2$ be an integer. Inspired by an observation of Erdős (1976), we investigate the behavior of $h_k(n)$, the number of $k$-full integers in the interval $(n^k, (n+1)^k)$ for positive integers $n$. Let $δ_k$ denote the supremum of the exponents $δ$ for which the inequality $h_k(n) > (\log n)^δ$ holds for infinitely many positive integers $n$. We improve the previously known lower bound $δ_k \ge 1/2$, implied by Munsch, Shparlinski, and Yau (2020), to $δ_k \ge 1$. Furthermore, for any given integer $m \ge 1$, we derive an effective upper bound for the smallest positive integer $n$ satisfying $h_k(n)\ge m$.

title: Extensions of $q$-supercongruences arising from a quadratic summation of Gasper and Rahman
summary: In this paper, inspired by recent work of Guo and Zhao, and of Guo and Zudilin, we establish two parametric extensions of their $q$-supercongruences using Gasper and Rahman's quadratic summation, the Chinese remainder theorem, and the creative microscoping method. These extensions yield two one-parameter generalizations of the $q$-supercongruences considered by Guo and Zhao and by Guo and Zudilin.

title: On Erdős' last equation
summary: For a positive integer $n\ge 2$, we look at the number of solutions of the Diophantine equation $$ n(x_1+\cdots+x_n)=x_1\cdots x_n. $$ Denoting by $f(n)$ this number we show that $\liminf_{n\to\infty} \log f(n)/\log n=0$.

title: Some notes on Erdős' last equation
summary: We study the Diophantine equation $$n^h(x_1 + \ldots + x_n) = x_1 x_2 \cdots x_n,$$ where $h \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, and $x_1 \le \ldots \le x_n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$. We define the solution set $ELE(h, n)$ consisting of all such integer tuples. We derive bounds on $x_n$ and $x_{n-1}$ in $ELE(h,n)$. We prove that $x_1 \cdot\ldots\cdot x_n \le n^h(n^h + 1)(n^h + n - 1)$. We also show that for $h = 1$, $x_{n-1} \le n + \max_{d \mid 2n^2 - 2n,\, d \le \sqrt{2n^2 - 2n}} d$, and for $h \ge 2$, the inequality $x_{n-1} \le 2n^h$ holds in $ELE(h, n)$. Moreover, we study the minimal value $g(h, n)$ of the largest coordinate $x_n$, and define $g(h) = \min_{n \ge 2} g(h,n)$. We prove that $$ \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{g(h,n)}{\frac{\log \log n \cdot \log \log \log \log n}{\log \log \log n}} \ge 1. $$ We also estimate the growth of the number of solutions. We show that for any $\varepsilon > 0,$ we have $\sum_{m \le n} |ELE(h,m)| < n^{h+1+\varepsilon} $ for sufficiently large $n$, and that $|ELE(h,n)| > n^{1 - \varepsilon}$ for infinitely many $n$.
journal_ref: Res. Number Theory 11 (2025), no. 4, Paper No. 94, 15 pp

title: A note on finite length for $\mathrm{GL}_2$
summary: Let $p>2$ be a prime and $F/\mathbf{Q}_p$ be a finite extension. We prove that every admissible smooth mod $p$ representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$, with a central character, and satisfying a Casimir annihilation condition, has finite length.

title: Affine pairs of minimizing units in totally real non-Galois cubic fields
summary: Let $Γ$ be a rank-two subgroup of the integral norm-one units in a totally real non-Galois cubic field. We prove that two distinct affinely equivalent minima of Godwin's spread on $Γ\setminus\{1\}$ generate $Γ$ and determine its complete minimum set: a pair with sum $\pm2$ or a triple of integral translates of product one. Every minimum generates the order $\mathbb{Z}[Γ]$. For an order whose norm-one units have such a pair, the order generated by its units is the smallest suborder with the same minimum value. We also give explicit families and a maximal order with minima in two distinct affine classes.

title: The least Carmichael numbers with $k$ prime factors
summary: Let $S_k$ denote the least Carmichael number with exactly $k$ prime factors. Like the later searches of Pinch, our algorithm builds the prime factors of a candidate in increasing order and stops as soon as the preproduct $P$ satisfies $Pλ(P) > B$. At that point there is at most one possible cofactor, and we recover all of its prime factors at once in polynomial time. We prove an unconditional bound on the number of candidates the search examines, in terms of how far $B$ exceeds the product of the first $k$ primes. When the search is run in doubling passes, this gives a running time of $e^{O(k)} = S_k^{O(1/\log k)}$ under a natural conjecture on the size of $S_k$. We also show that the constant in the exponent is sharp for the set of square-free numbers that the bound counts. Finally, we compute $S_k$ for every $k \leq 64$; Pinch had computed it for $k \leq 35$.

title: Multivariable $(\varphi, N)$-modules and $(\varphi, N_\nabla)$-modules
summary: The goal of this article is to introduce the category of effective filtered multivariable $(\varphi, N)$-modules and the category of multivariable $(\varphi, N_\nabla)$-modules of finite $E_Δ$-height over the rigid-analytic open polydisk $\mathcal{O}_Δ$, and to establish an exact tensor equivalence between them. This generalizes Kisin's analytic classification of filtered $(\varphi, N)$-modules and provides the rigid-analytic foundation for multivariable $p$-adic Hodge theory.

title: On the invariants of L-functions of degree 2, II: twisted conductor
summary: We continue our study of the invariants of the $L$-functions of deree 2 twisted by Dirichlet characters. In a previous paper, we proved that twisting does not change degree and internal shift. Our aim now is to show a corresponding theorem for the conductor. This paper is intended as the second part of a series aiming to prove a general version of the Weil converse theorem with minimal assumptions on the shape of the functional equation of twists.

title: Explicit Tartakowsky theorem and universality criterion sets over totally real number fields
summary: We prove an explicit version of Tartakowsky's theorem over all totally real number fields. Namely, a positive definite integral lattice of rank at least five represents every totally positive integer that it represents locally, provided that the norm of the integer exceeds an explicit bound, exponential in powers of the volume of the lattice and of the discriminant of the field. As an application, we give explicit criterion sets for universal quadratic forms over all but finitely many real quadratic fields. Finally, we determine the minimal criterion sets for an infinite family of real quadratic fields.

title: Néron Functions on Jacobians of Odd-Degree Hyperelliptic Curves
summary: We express Néron functions on Jacobians of odd-degree hyperelliptic curves of arbitrary genus in terms of admissible pairings, using the pullback of the theta divisor via a generalized Abel--Jacobi morphism. Over non-archimedean local fields, we relate Néron functions to local Néron pairings on the curve and, moreover, deduce a comparison between unramified $p$-adic Néron functions and unramified local Coleman--Gross height functions. Furthermore, we decompose the Néron function into an intersection term $I$ and a Green function term $T$, and compute $T$ for specific semistable reduction types. We compare our decomposition with other decompositions in the literature.

title: Sums of Integers with Small Prime Factors
summary: Let $P^+(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$, with $P^+(1)=1$. We prove that, for every $β>103/(256\sqrt e)$, there is a constant $C=C(β)>0$ such that every sufficiently large integer $N$ can be written as $N=a+b$, where $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ and $$ P^+(a)\leq N^β,\qquad P^+(b)\leq(\log N)^C. $$ This strengthens Balog's result, which gives two $N^β$-smooth summands for $β>4/(9\sqrt e)$. The proof combines Balog's argument with convolution estimates that are uniform in the residue class.

title: Cassini ovals, translated polynomials, and the arithmetic of their discriminants and resultants
summary: For a polynomial $f$, $a>0$ and $b,ω\in\mathbb{C}$, consider the translate $J^{(a,b,ω)}f(z)=f(z/a)-ωf(b/a)$. We show that for $f(x)=(x^{2}-1)^{n}$ and $ω=\pm1$ every zero of $J^{(a,b,ω)}f$ lies on the Cassini oval $|z^{2}-a^{2}|=|b^{2}-a^{2}|$. We call these translates \emph{Cassini polynomials} and give their zeros explicitly, prove that the zeros for $ω=1$ and $ω=-1$ strictly interlace on each component of the oval, and evaluate their discriminants and resultants in closed form. We then prove the reduced monic polynomials $Q_{n}=a^{2n}J^{(a,b,ω)}f/(z^{2}-b^{2})$ factor into homogenized cyclotomic polynomials, satisfying $\operatorname{Res}(Q_{m},Q_{n})=(b^{2}-a^{2})^{2(m-1)(n-1)}$ for coprime $m,n$, and have discriminants governed by a Lucas sequence. We then prove a comparison principle: if $f$ is even or odd with all zeros in $[-1,1]$, $b\in\mathbb{R}$ and $|ω|\le1$, then every zero of $J^{(a,ib,ω)}f$ satisfies $|z^{2}-a^{2}|\le a^{2}+b^{2}$, and the symmetry hypothesis cannot be removed. As an application, every solution of $\det(A(P_{n})-λI)=F_{n+1}$, where $A(P_{n})$ is the adjacency matrix of the path on $n$ vertices and $F_{n+1}$ is a Fibonacci number, satisfies $|λ^{2}-4|\le5$. This disproves, for every $n$, a conjecture of Gullerud, Johnson and Mbirika that the real parts of these solutions are unbounded.

title: Zeta Functions of Polygonal Numbers: Analytic Continuation, Poles and Zero Scattering
summary: We study the Zeta functions associated with polygonal numbers, focusing on their meromorphic continuation, poles, residues, and trivial zeros. We then investigate the distribution of their nontrivial zeros. Under explicit hypotheses, we derive an asymptotic formula for the mean real part of zeros in long height windows. The formula predicts convergence of this mean to 1/4 as the height tends to infinity. We also formulate a stronger concentration conjecture and examine numerical evidence for it.

title: Sumsets modulo ideals: Baire category and descriptive complexity
summary: Given an ideal $\mathcal I$ on the nonnegative integers, we study the family $Σ(\mathcal I)$ of all sets for which every $\mathcal{I}$-small modification is not a nontrivial sumset $A+B$. We prove that $Σ(\mathcal I)$ is comeager whenever $\mathcal{I}$ is an Erdős--Ulam ideal generated by a nonincreasing sequence of positive weights. This answers an open question for the ideal $\mathcal{Z}$ of asymptotic density zero sets in [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. \textbf{151} (2023), 3681--3689]. We also show that $Σ(\mathcal I)$ is either empty or a dense $G_δ$-complete set whenever $\mathcal{I}$ is an $F_σ$ ideal which is invariant under finite modifications. This implies that the family of nontrivial sumsets $A+B$ is $F_σ$-complete (hence, Borel). On the other hand, we construct a meager ideal $\mathcal{I}$ for which $Σ(\mathcal I)$ is neither meager nor comeager. Finally, we prove that $Σ(\mathcal Z)$ is coanalytic and not $F_{σδ}$.

title: On elliptic curves with prescribed analytic rank at least $2$
summary: Zywina recently showed that infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ have rank $2$, settling a long-standing open question. We explore the analytic version of this problem, showing that every elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ has infinitely many quadratic twists with analytic rank either $2$ or $4$, subject to GRH. We also obtain, under the same assumption, infinitely many congruent number curves with odd analytic rank between $3$ and $17$.

title: Complex Moments of the Derivative of the Riemann Zeta Function
summary: We investigate the complex moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function through a random Euler product model. For each fixed $σ>1/2$ and every $s\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$, we show, under the Lindelöf hypothesis, that the $2s$-th moment of $|ζ'(σ+\mathrm{i}t)|$ over $t\in[1,T]$ converges, as $T\to\infty$, to the corresponding moment of the derivative of the random Euler product. We then establish, unconditionally, an asymptotic formula for the latter moment as $σ\downarrow 1/2$ throughout the half-plane $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$. For positive real moments, our approach is based on a change-of-measure argument and a Gaussian limit theorem for the logarithmic derivative under a tilted probability measure. For general complex moments, we combine Fourier analysis of weighted complex measures with regularized Riesz distributions. As an application, under the Lindelöf hypothesis, we resolve the conjecture of Simm and Wei [J. Lond. Math. Soc. 113 (2026)] on the complex moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function for every $s\in\mathbb C$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$. We establish the predicted asymptotic formula as $σ\downarrow1/2$, with the leading order $s^2+2s$ and an explicit leading coefficient involving an arithmetic factor and the confluent hypergeometric function of the first kind. The conjecture also holds unconditionally when $\operatorname{Re}(s)\in (0,2)$.

title: On complemented skew braces
summary: We investigate complemented skew left braces, that is, skew braces in which every skew subbrace admits a complement. We establish that if every minimal subbrace of a finite skew brace is complemented, then the brace is supersoluble and all its skew subbraces of prime power order are elementary abelian. We also show that the converse does not hold in general, providing a finite counterexample. Furthermore, we prove that every subbrace of a finite direct product of square-free skew braces is complemented. Finally, we extend our investigation to the infinite setting, proving that every multipermutational complemented skew brace is hypercyclic and that all its skew subbraces whose additive groups are $p$-groups are elementary abelian.

title: On Block-Primitive Combinatorial Designs
summary: We settle a long-standing problem by proving that every block-primitive combinatorial design is point-primitive. Since block-primitivity and point-primitivity coincide for symmetric designs by duality, it remains to treat the non-symmetric $2$-designs. For these we apply the O'Nan--Scott theorems for primitive and for quasiprimitive permutation groups and prove that the automorphism group of every such design is almost simple on points and on blocks. Together with the classification of finite simple groups, this classifies all non-symmetric block-primitive $2$-designs except for two families of block stabilizers in even characteristic. The exceptions are as follows. One family is of subfield type, $PSL_2(q_0)$ with $q=q_0^{d}$, $d\geq2$, of order below the dihedral point stabilizer $D_{2(q\pm1)}$, and includes $S_3\cong PSL_2(2)$ and $A_5\cong PSL_2(4)$. The other is the dihedral block stabilizer $D_{2(q-1)}$, where the block is a union of $a$ of the $q/2$ orbits, so that $v=q(q-1)/2$, $k=a(q-1)$ and $λ=2a(aq-a-1)/(q-2)$, the last an integer exactly when $(q-2)/2$ divides $a(a-1)$; this family is exhausted by finite enumeration except at the degrees beyond its range. We then determine which of these designs have strength $t\geq 3$. Apart from the inversive planes and the five Witt designs, exactly two Steiner families arise, attached to the exceptional maximal subgroups of $PGL_2(q)$. There is no non-complete design of strength $t\geq 6$.

title: Orbital graph structure of alternating full groups and simple torsion amenable groups of exponential growth
summary: We develop a framework for constructing simple alternating full groups A(G, X), associated with finite fragmentations of minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions, with controlled orbital-graph codings and purely non-Hausdorff singularities. We also prove that positive entropy of a naturally labeled admissible orbital line forces exponential word growth of the acting group. As an application, we construct continuum many pairwise abstractly nonisomorphic, finitely generated, infinite, simple, torsion, amenable groups of exponential word growth. They arise as alternating full groups of fragmented minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions with linearly repetitive generic regular orbital graphs and purely non-Hausdorff singularities. Under the same minimality, expansivity, linear repetitivity and singularity assumptions, if every finite clopen coding is determined by a bounded fragmentation window, the alternating full group has intermediate word growth.

title: A counterexample to the subgraphings approximate the cost problem
summary: We prove that for every $k\ge 2$, the free group $\mathbb{F}_k$ on $k$ generators admits a finite generating set $S$ such that the Schreier graphing of the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{F}_k$ with respect to $S$ does not admit spanning subgraphings that would approximate the cost of the action. In particular, this gives an example of a graphing that spans a treeable countable pmp equivalence relation, but does not admit a spanning subtreeing.

title: The unitary group $U_3(4)$ as a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$
summary: We prove that the simple unitary group $U_3(4)=\operatorname{PSU}_3(\mathbb{F}_4)$, of order $62400$, is the Galois group of a regular extension of $\mathbb{Q}(t)$, and hence of infinitely many extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$. The extension has four branch points, with inertia groups of orders $2$, $2$, $3$, $3$, and it is the only extension with these properties up to a rational change of the coordinate $t$. We give an explicit polynomial of degree $65$ for it.
comment: 28 pages, 2 figures; the polynomials and the programs of the proofs are included as ancillary files

title: The monoid of orientation preserving mappings on a chain
summary: We introduce new kinds of regular monoids of transformations consisting of mappings which preserve or reverse the orientation of a finite cycle.

title: Centralizers in Catalan Monoids
summary: Fix a chain $X_n=\{1<\cdots<n\}$, where $n$ is a positive integer. The Catalan monoid $\mathcal{C}_n$ consists of all decreasing and order-preserving transformations of $X_n$, with function composition as the operation. For $β\in\mathcal{C}_n$, its centralizer is $C(β)=\{α\in\mathcal{C}_n:αβ=βα\}$. We characterize the elements of $C(\varepsilon)$, $C(μ)$, and $C(β)$, where $\varepsilon\in\mathcal{C}_n$ is an idempotent, $μ\in\mathcal{C}_n$ is a nilpotent, and $β\in\mathcal{C}_n$ is a general element. For an idempotent $\varepsilon\in\mathcal{C}_n$, we derive formulas for the cardinality of $C(\varepsilon)$, as well as formulas for the numbers of idempotents and nilpotents of $C(\varepsilon)$. We relate indexing sets arising in these formulas to Dyck paths and Narayana numbers. For a nilpotent $μ\in\mathcal{C}_n$, we present algorithms that construct $C(μ)$, its subset of idempotents, and its subsemigroup of nilpotents, thereby determining their cardinalities. We also describe the nilpotents whose centralizers consist only of idempotents, of nilpotents together with the identity, or of nilpotents and idempotents. We extend these descriptions to arbitrary elements of $\mathcal{C}_n$. To obtain our results, we represent $β\in\mathcal{C}_n$ as a sequence $\langle T_1,\ldots,T_m\rangle$ of rooted trees. The sets of vertices of the trees form a partition of $X_n$. Each tree is level-ordered, which means that it can be drawn in such a way that moving from the root down, level by level, from left to right at each level, we pass through an increasing sequence of consecutive elements of $X_n$.

title: Average character degree below 14/3
summary: We prove that a finite group with average irreducible character degree less than $14/3$ is solvable if it has no chief factor isomorphic to $A_5$. This answers a question of Aziziheris and Eivazzadeh.

title: Finite presentations for Thompson monoids
summary: Thompson's group $V$ was introduced in 1965 as one of the first examples of an infinite finitely presented simple group. The Higman-Thompson groups $V_{k, r}$ naturally generalize $V$; they exhibit many of the same interesting properties and have been extensively studied in the literature. Monoid theoretic analogues $TV_{k, r}$, $PTV_{k, r}$, and $IV_{k, r}$ of the Higman-Thompson groups were first considered by Thompson, and published many years later in work of Birget. The monoid theoretic analogue of the symmetric group is the full transformation monoid, in that every monoid is isomorphic to a submonoid of some full transformation monoid. The analogous role for inverse monoids is played by the symmetric inverse monoid. Birget's three monoids $TV_{k, r}$, $PTV_{k, r}$, and $IV_{k, r}$ are to $V_{n, r}$ what the full, and partial transformation monoids, and the symmetric inverse monoid are to the symmetric group. The second author and De Witt recently showed that $TV_{k, r}$ is finitely presented. In this paper we show that the remaining two monoids $PTV_{k, r}$ and $IV_{k, r}$ are also finitely presented.

title: Expansion in powers of simple groups of Lie type
summary: We prove an expansion theorem for direct powers of all nonabelian finite simple groups $G$ other than the alternating groups and the Suzuki groups ${}^2B_2(q)$. If $G^m$ is generated by $d\ge2$ elements, then $G^m$ has a symmetric generating multiset of at most $Cd$ elements and normalized spectral gap at least $C^{-1}d^{-\log_2 3}$, for an absolute constant $C>0$. In particular, this answers a question of Sabatini on $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)^p$. For $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, we use the expander graphs constructed by Lubotzky--Samuels--Vishne, and an amplification trick for direct powers; in high rank, we use the Ershov--Jaikin-Zapirain property (T) theorem.
